cells.reason: Requires upper filesystem layers to route all metadata updates through logged transactions, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires mount and operator paths to run user-space recovery on a dirty log (`RCVR_MUSTRCVR`), which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.

States that the storage stack must report a ”failed write” as an error rather than returning ”success with a short transfer, wrong-sector read, or failed write while leaving B_ERROR clear,” matching E4's contract that ”disk: a completed write was actually stored (no lost writes).”

States (citing `recover.c:894`) that ”when the driver reports an I/O complete, that entire transfer is on stable storage and later reads, including reads after power loss, return those bytes” rather than sitting in a ”volatile write-back cache,” directly naming the completed-write durability and storage contracts of E2, E3, E4, and E5.
Requires callers to use the replacement buffer handle (`nbP`) returned by modifying operations, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires the configured device and aggregate block size to be a supported power of two matching the superblock, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires user-space `setjmp`/`longjmp` to preserve the return code passed to `longjmp`, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires log-creation callers to exclude concurrent activity on the device, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires the failure environment not to produce CRC-preserving corruption on log pages, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires callers to keep `newData` source memory stable while it is logged and copied into the buffer, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires operators to run the salvager rather than force an aggregate online after hard I/O or unrecoverable log errors, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.

Requires filesystem and VM allocation callers to record an undo-zero transaction and end it only after the first write completes, whereas E5 violates the disk's completed-write durability contract after the caller properly orders `OFILL` before `END`.
Requires periodic OS sync/checkpoint activity to bound the active log tail, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires the log container's size and block allocation to remain fixed while the aggregate is in use, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.

Requires VM strategy callers to invoke `elbb_UndoZero` with the right byte range and wait for write completion before ending the transaction, whereas E5 is a violation of the disk durability contract rather than caller omission.
Requires callers to keep each transaction within `MAX_TRAN_SIZE` and split oversized operations, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires `fsync` callers to tag or list all relevant buffers and flush VM pages, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.

Requires callers to use redo-only initialization (`elbb_Initialize`/`CreateBlock`) only on newly allocated blocks whose old contents need not be restored, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires the log-location array to list distinct preallocated log blocks that do not overlap file or metadata blocks, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires transaction package initialization to run single-threaded before concurrent use, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires storage writes to affect only the addressed sectors without misdirected overwrites of unrelated blocks, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires the VM and vnode layers to respect the strategy layer's bound on simultaneous waiters per in-transit block, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires callers not to mix logged and unlogged modifications on the same buffer, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires callers of `elbb_LogInit` to have no dirty cached buffers for the device when recovery may run, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires operators to leave removable media in place until aggregate close finishes writing the restart block, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires callers needing persistence to select a synchronous wait mode rather than `elbb_async`, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires log-creation callers not to hold buffer-package locks upon entry, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires log length and page indices to fit within 16-bit offset and signed-distance arithmetic, whereas E7 is an internal pass-number invariant (`own`) rather than a log-size configuration contract.
Requires the OS clock to progress normally for buffer-cache aging heuristics, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires hardware sector writes to be atomic and large enough to hold the log page header and checksum, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires upper layers to place transaction boundaries so that each committed transaction preserves filesystem invariants, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires pointer alignment macros not to truncate addresses on the target architecture, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires backup/restore and split log/data device deployments to keep the log and data devices paired and recovered together, which is not the single-disk durability or lost-write contract of E2–E5.

States that ”until Episode overwrites a block, the device returns the bytes of the last completed write to that block” and forbids ”a dropped write that was acknowledged” or ”dropped sector,” naming E4's contract that ”disk: a completed write was actually stored (no lost writes)” and overlapping with E2, E3, and E5's completed-write durability contract.
Requires initialization callers to provide a valid writable buffer pool for the package's lifetime, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
Requires external callers to request only data or logged buffer types and leave internal types to `logbuf`, which is not the violated contract of any sealed bug.
